question: Explain why a ferromagnetic material can be converted into a strong magnet, while a diamagnetic material cannot. Relate your answer to magnetic moment and material behaviour in an external magnetic field.

options.A: Ferromagnetic materials have domains whose atomic magnetic moments can align in an external field, producing strong magnetisation. Diamagnetic materials develop only a very weak induced magnetic moment opposite to the applied field, so they cannot become strong magnets.
options.B: Diamagnetic materials become strong magnets because their induced magnetic moment is large and along the applied field, while ferromagnetic domains oppose the field.
options.C: Both ferromagnetic and diamagnetic materials become equally strong magnets because all materials have the same magnetic moment in an external field.
options.D: Ferromagnetic materials cannot be magnetised because their domains remain permanently random, while diamagnetic materials have permanent aligned domains.
